title: Sturge-Weber Syndrome: The Ocular Nexus
summary: Sturge-Weber Syndrome (SWS), or encephalotrigeminal angiomatosis, is a phakomatosis characterized by a facial port-wine stain and associated vascular malformations in the brain and eyes, most notably diffuse choroidal hemangioma.

sections.title: Definition & Etiology
sections.content: SWS is a sporadic neurocutaneous disorder. Etiology is linked to a somatic mosaic mutation in the GNAQ gene (c.548G>A) on chromosome 9q21. This results in constitutive activation of the MAPK/ERK pathway, leading to capillary/venous malformations.

sections.title: Clinical Features: The Triad
content: 1. Port-wine stain (nevus flammeus) typically involving the V1/V2 trigeminal distribution.
2. Leptomeningeal angioma (ipsilateral to facial stain), causing seizures, hemiparesis, and intellectual impairment.
3. Ocular involvement: Diffuse choroidal hemangioma (DCH) and Glaucoma.

sections.title: The 'Tomato Ketchup' Fundus
content: Diffuse choroidal hemangioma presents as a thickened, deep red-orange choroid.
Loss of the normal choroidal tessellation.
Secondary exudative retinal detachment (often bullous).
Cystoid macular edema (CME) as a chronic sequela.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to refer
content: Ipsilateral V1 port-wine stain (high risk for ocular involvement).
Acute onset of bullous exudative retinal detachment.
Refractory glaucoma unresponsive to topical medical therapy.
New-onset seizures or focal neurological deficits.

sections.title: Diagnostic Protocol
content: Step 1: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy with goniometry to assess for angle anomalies.
Step 2: Indirect ophthalmoscopy for the 'tomato ketchup' fundus appearance.
Step 3: B-scan Ultrasonography (crucial for verifying posterior segment thickening).
Step 4: Fundus Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) to show patchy hyperfluorescence/staining.
Step 5: OCT (EDI-OCT) to quantify choroidal thickness and subretinal fluid.

sections.title: Management of DCH
content: Observation for asymptomatic cases.
Photodynamic Therapy (PDT) with Verteporfin: Standard for symptomatic fluid.
Anti-VEGF intravitreal injections (adjunctive).
External beam radiotherapy (reserved for severe/refractory cases).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Avoid filtering surgery in SWS glaucoma if possible due to high risk of massive choroidal effusion/hemorrhage from low intraocular pressure.
Consider goniotomy or trabeculotomy for early-onset cases.
The choroidal hemangioma is benign, but its exudative nature threatens vision; treat the fluid, not just the lesion.
Monitor episcleral hemangioma as a clinical marker for glaucoma severity.
